conventions.convention: Signature is (-,+,+,+); R(X,Y)Z = ∇X∇YZ − ∇Y∇XZ − ∇[X,Y]Z, with R(∂c,∂d)∂b = Rᵃ_bcd ∂a and Ric_bd = g^ac R_abcd.

Counterterm tensors pair with compactly supported inverse-metric variations with positive sign. First variations integrate pointwise density derivatives; finite total actions and finite-parameter action differences are unnecessary.

The stress contract supplies a common state-independent subtraction kernel, finite-order bidifferential operator, overlap convention, scale and local curvature correction. Smooth remainders are differentiated before taking coincidence limits.
Hadamard positive-frequency covectors are future null; their base points may occur in either parameter order along the connecting future-directed null geodesic.
Use SI units and length coordinates x⁰ = ct: stress has units J m⁻³, curvature has units m⁻², curvature-squared variation tensors have units m⁻⁴, and their equation couplings have units m².
The emitter comparison assumes Countable Choice, positive constants, 0 < η ≤ 1 and 0 < M_min < M₀; its interval includes both endpoints and retains positive mass.

load_bearing.statement: Supply a positive normalized Hadamard state, local state-independent Hμ with Wω − Hμ smooth, a finite-order D_ab and fixed local C_ab; define T^ren_ab by the coincidence limit of D_ab(Wω − Hμ) plus C_ab, requiring overlap compatibility, local covariance and conservation. No general existence or parametrix construction is asserted.

Adopt G_ab + Λ_cc g_ab + α_ct H^(R²)_ab + β_ct H^(Ric²)_ab = (8πG/c⁴) T^ren_ab[g,ω] on the supplied admissible domain below E_cut, with fixed couplings, state, renormalization prescription and retarded data. No solution existence, uniqueness, stability or physical applicability is asserted.

Supply smooth symmetric covariant tensors whose pairings with every compactly supported inverse-metric variation equal the integrated pointwise first derivatives of the scalar-curvature-squared and Ricci-squared densities, with positive sign.

For two positive Hadamard states of the same scalar Klein–Gordon operator on one fixed background, using an identical prescription, the stress difference equals the coincidence limit of D_ab(Wω₁ − Wω₂); this biscalar difference is smooth. Common state-independent local curvature additions cancel.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact curvature operator, component ordering, Ricci contraction, scalar curvature and Einstein tensor conventions.
The exact Countable Choice hypothesis carried by the emitter diagnostic example.
The emitter ODE, positive cube-root solution, coefficient α and positive-mass cutoff underlying the diagnostic supplier.
The crossing-time and dimensionless quasistatic diagnostic definitions used by the published bound.
The exact diagnostic formula and uniform positive-cutoff bound cited by the assigned example; its scope explicitly excludes a coupled backreaction error estimate.

concerns.concern: The local-covariance clause quantifies over every time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding with causally convex image, but the contract independently supplies P = −g^ab∇a∇b + V for arbitrary smooth real V. It does not require the embedding to preserve V or intertwine the selected operators. Since Hμ and the prescription depend on P, metric preservation alone does not identify the data being pulled back. State the compatibility requirement P ψ* = ψ* P′, equivalently V = ψ*V′ in this setting, and clarify the corresponding state restriction when comparing stress expectations.

seams_checked.note: The stress contract uses the collapse supplier for its scalar-field and positive-state specialization, while explicitly declining to impose Schwarzschild geometry or scattering assumptions on the general contract. No Hawking occupation result is promoted to a coupled solution.

The variation definition uses smooth finite-parameter field families and ordinary parameter derivatives consistently with the supplier; it assumes no infinite-dimensional configuration-space manifold.

The horizon postulate explicitly selects zero curvature-squared couplings, translates SI constants and cutoff dimensions to its natural units, supplies its state family and regularity, and adopts first-order focusing separately. It does not attribute a higher-curvature focusing theorem or solution existence to the supplier.

The open problem uses the fixed-coupling equation and Hadamard prescription as formulation inputs and selects an actually existing solution as problem data. It does not claim that the suppliers construct that solution or establish continuum entropy limits.
The logical-firewall remark accurately describes the equation as an effective adopted model below a supplied cutoff, without existence, uniqueness or stability guarantees.
